opex.name: Research & development, net
opex.note: The engineers building Neutron and the next generation of spacecraft — the company's biggest single expense, 37% of revenue. Up 39%. R&D alone is bigger than gross profit, which is why the company loses money.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, offices, admin. Up 55% as the company scales.

follow100Note: The striking thing: R&D alone eats $36.73 of every $100 — more than the entire gross profit. Rocket Lab is a development-stage company that happens to sell rockets; the business only works if Neutron and the backlog convert into much bigger, higher-margin revenue later. Meanwhile, the $4.4B cash pile already earns $10.69 per $100 of revenue in interest — a side business in its own right.
footerNote: Chart note: Rocket Lab's running costs exceeded its gross profit, so the chart draws the $79.677M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source that funds the operating gap and the $3.503M tax bill — the shortfall came from the balance sheet, not from revenue.
oneTimers: Loss on extinguishment of debt ($27.3M): a one-time charge for retiring the convertible senior notes early — the balance sheet shows convertible notes down to $1.3M from $152.4M at Dec 31, 2025. Without this charge, the net loss would have been ~$52M instead of ~$80M.

Transaction costs ($21.3M in Q3; $31.6M in nine months): deal costs for the pending acquisition of Iridium Communications — the company says it is now fully funded (via the ATM equity offering) and Iridium shareholders have overwhelmingly approved it. These costs are excluded from Adjusted EBITDA and non-GAAP opex.

The ATM equity offering ($3.91B raised in nine months): Rocket Lab sold a large block of new shares at-the-market, which is why cash jumped from $828.7M (Dec 31, 2025) to $4,447.7M and the share count rose to ~652M weighted-average shares (from ~529M a year ago). The cash funds the Iridium acquisition and Neutron development — but existing shareholders were diluted by roughly 23%.
Stock-based compensation ($18.3M in Q3; $66.0M in nine months): excluded from Adjusted EBITDA, but a real cost to shareholders.

The tax swing: Q3 2025 included a $41.1M tax benefit (deferred tax assets), while Q3 2026 has a $3.5M tax expense — a $44.6M year-over-year swing that explains most of why the net loss quadrupled while the operating loss widened only 34%.
otherDetail: $28.627M of interest income, less a $27.259M one-time debt-extinguishment charge and $0.323M of interest expense, plus a $0.473M foreign-exchange gain and $1.497M of other income — net $3.015M.

segments.name: Product revenues
segments.note: Rockets, spacecraft and components sold as hardware — Electron launches, satellite platforms and parts. Nearly doubled (+90%) and now 74% of revenue.

segments.name: Service revenues
segments.note: Launch services, mission operations and related work billed as services rather than hardware. Up 38%.

takeaways.text: $3.57B, up 52% in a single quarter, with 117 launches booked and Neutron already sold out 16 missions deep at up to $70M a launch — before it has ever flown. Demand is not the constraint; execution is.
takeaways.title: The backlog is the story

takeaways.text: The operating loss grew $20M on Neutron R&D, and the net loss quadrupled mostly because of a $27.3M one-time debt charge and a $44.6M tax swing vs last year. Adjusted EBITDA loss actually narrowed to −$18.0M, and operating cash flow turned positive (+$7.2M) for the first time.
takeaways.title: The loss widened, but look at why

takeaways.text: The ATM offering raised $3.9B to fund Iridium and Neutron, but the share count is up ~23% year over year. The question for shareholders is whether that cash buys a second business (Iridium) and a bigger rocket (Neutron) that earn their keep.
takeaways.title: A $4.4 billion war chest — paid for with dilution

verdict: Rocket Lab posted a record $268 million quarter with its backlog up 52% to $3.6 billion, but it still lost $80 million as Neutron development spending outran revenue — and the balance sheet now holds $4.4 billion in cash after a $3.9 billion share sale to fund the Iridium deal.
